key_insight: HalluGuard presents a unified, model-agnostic framework that separates and detects two distinct hallucination sources—data-driven and reasoning-driven—using a single risk-oriented approach, improving generalization beyond task-specific heuristics.
problem_solved: Detecting and distinguishing hallucinations in LLM outputs is brittle because existing methods target only one hallucination source or rely on task-specific rules, limiting reliability in high-stakes domains.
method: Taxonomy + risk framing: formally separate data-driven (factual/knowledge gaps) and reasoning-driven (chain-of-thought/logic errors) hallucinations and define a unified Hallucination Risk score.

Dual-check pipeline: combine retrieval- and evidence-based factual verification for data-driven errors with chain-of-thought consistency/self-verification and contradiction-detection for reasoning-driven errors.
Model-agnostic evaluation & calibration: apply the risk estimator across tasks and LLMs, calibrate thresholds, and validate detection/mitigation performance on multi-domain benchmarks.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical, generalizable toolset to detect and prioritize hallucination risks across models and tasks, enabling safer deployment and targeted mitigation strategies in high-stakes applications.

paper_title: HalluGuard: Demystifying Data-Driven and Reasoning-Driven Hallucinations in LLMs
paper_authors: Xinyue Zeng, Junhong Lin, Yujun Yan, Feng Guo, Liang Shi
